rationale: The whole chain traces to one uuid advisory (a missing buffer bounds check), reached through google-gax, gaxios, retry-request, and teeny-request. firebase-admin and firebase-functions are already pinned to their latest release inside the declared major (13.10.0 and 6.6.0). npm's proposed fix is firebase-admin@10.3.0, an older major version -- a downgrade, not a fix. No forward-compatible release resolves the transitive uuid chain yet. Tracked upstream; re-check when firebase-admin publishes a 13.x or 14.x patch.

react-router-dom is already at 6.30.6, the latest release inside the declared ^6.30.1 range. The fix requires react-router-dom@7.18.2, a major-version rewrite of the router API. Scheduling that migration separately from this audit pass.

apps/web pins vite@^5.4.19 and is already at 5.4.21, the last 5.x release ever published. The fix needs vite@6.4.3 or later, a major upgrade with breaking config and plugin API changes. Vite only runs the local dev server and the build step; it never ships to a deployed environment or handles untrusted input in production. Not blocking CI under the production-only audit policy.

firebase-tools carries no advisory of its own; its high severity comes from bundled tar (see the tar entry below) plus a transitive uuid finding. It is a devDependency used only to run local emulators and to deploy from a developer or release machine; it never ships in a deployed artifact. Pinned to ^14.11.1 and already at 14.27.0, the newest 14.x release. The fix is firebase-tools@15.28.1, a major upgrade. Scheduling that upgrade and its migration notes separately.

tar is a transitive devDependency pulled in by firebase-tools, only used to unpack CLI/emulator archives on a developer or release machine; it is never a runtime dependency of a deployed function or the web app. The fix requires the same firebase-tools@15.28.1 major upgrade tracked above. Scheduling together with that migration.
